title: Phase Signal File
description: Schema for ~/catalyst/execution-core/workers/{TICKET}/phase-{name}.json — the per-phase coordination file written by the execution-core daemon and updated by phase-agent workers. The daemon dispatches work by writing this file; the phase-agent worker updates it (status, bg_job_id) as it runs; the daemon reads it to determine when to advance to the next phase.

ticket.description: Linear ticket identifier (e.g. 'CTL-123'). Matches the worker directory name.

phase.description: Name of the pipeline phase this signal file represents.

model.description: Claude model string passed to the phase-agent worker at dispatch time (e.g. 'opus', 'sonnet'). Determined by resolving Layer-1 and Layer-2 phaseAgents.models config.

turnCap.description: Maximum number of agent turns allowed for this phase invocation. When reached, the phase-agent emits status 'turn-cap-exhausted' and halts.

status.description: Current lifecycle status of this phase, written by the daemon on dispatch and updated by the phase-agent as work progresses. NOTE: this enum is known to be INCOMPLETE — the runtime also writes at least `needs-input`, `preempted` and `aborted`, which are absent here (tracked separately). A schema that rejects valid production signals is worse than none, so treat a failure against this enum as a schema gap until proven otherwise.

yieldedAt.description: CTL-1854. When the current yield EPISODE began (status `awaiting-work`). Set once and preserved across re-yields — it is deliberately NOT rewritten per declaration, because that let a re-yield extend a short deadline (a 60s wait re-declared after 30s expired at 90). Absent unless the phase is, or recently was, yielded.

firstYieldedAt.description: CTL-1854. When the agent declared the FIRST yield of the current episode; preserved across re-yields. The 30-minute ceiling is measured from here, not from `yieldedAt`, so repeatedly re-yielding cannot extend the wait. A present-but-unparseable value is treated as expired, never as a fresh anchor.

yieldMs.description: CTL-1854. Optional per-yield window in milliseconds, from `--yield-seconds`. Clamped to the 30-minute ceiling — an agent may request LESS, never more — and MONOTONIC: a re-yield takes the minimum of the existing and requested windows, and never clears it. Absent means use the ceiling.

bg_job_id.description: 8-character hex identifier of the Claude Code bg job running this phase. Written by the phase-agent at startup. Used for orphan detection and revive deduplication. null before the worker writes it or after a terminal status.

worktreePath.description: Absolute filesystem path to the git worktree created for this ticket/phase. null for phases that do not create a worktree (e.g. monitor-merge, monitor-deploy, teardown on some configurations).

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the daemon dispatched this phase (i.e. when the signal file was first written).

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last write to this signal file. The orphan reaper compares this against the current time to detect stalled workers.

completedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the phase reached a terminal status (done, failed, skipped, turn-cap-exhausted). null while still in progress.

failureReason.description: Short description of why the phase failed, written by phase-agent-emit-complete when --status failed is passed. Omit (null) on success — do not pass --reason to emit-complete on successful phases.

stallClass.description: CTL-2158. The stall's ONE class, written by the escalation producers via stall-class.mjs::classifyStall. "system" = provider overload, rate/account limits, connectivity, executor death, retry/cycle caps, an untidy working copy, orphan-sweep staleness — retry with backoff, and if persistent ONE fleet alert, never a per-ticket artifact. "ask" = a scope/priority/approval/credential decision only a person can take — one ask ticket carrying `blocks`. "moot" = already done, superseded, no actionable plan — close. "held" = the classifier could not prove any of the three (or the evidence pointed two ways): HELD FOR REVIEW, never dropped, never auto-retried forever, never auto-cleared. Additive — `status` and `stalledReason` keep their CTL-1552 values.

stallClassRule.description: CTL-2158. WHICH rule produced stallClass, so a verdict can be audited rather than trusted: `exact:<reason>`, `prefix:<prefix>`, `family:<class>`, `signal:stallClass`, `ambiguous:<a>+<b>`, `manufactured-escalation`, `no-reason`, or `unclassified`.

stallClassManufactured.description: CTL-2158. True when the escalation's explanation came from escalation-explanation.mjs::coerceExplanation's degrade branch (`degraded:true`) — i.e. the human-facing prose is a template ("priority call the agent cannot make unilaterally"), not a real question. Present so a board can say the ask was generated. A manufactured explanation NEVER promotes a stall to `ask`.

escalationPublished.description: CTL-2158. Set by the producers that publish a COMPLETE escalation (label + brief + Linear comment): recovery-emit, recovery-reasoning, recovery.mjs::markEscalationCapTerminal, boot-resume's expired approval gate. unstuck-sweep's quiet-gate keys on this instead of on `stalledReason === "needs_human"`, so a ticket a human is already holding never receives a second authored comment once that token is deleted. ⛔ It is deliberately NOT inferred from the presence of `explanation`: scheduler.mjs's generic stall writer attaches a coerced explanation to EVERY stall it records, so inferring it would silence the sweep's repair actions wholesale.

attentionReason.description: Human-readable explanation written when the daemon escalates the ticket to needs-human status. null during normal operation.

handoffPath.description: Absolute path to a phase artifact (e.g. research doc, plan doc, verify.json) passed to downstream phases as context. Written by the phase-agent at completion.

catalystSessionId.description: Catalyst session identifier (not the Claude Code session UUID). Used by the session tracker to correlate cost and duration metrics in catalyst.db.

pr.description: Pull request metadata written by the pr phase-agent after opening a PR. Only present on phase-pr signal files.

phaseTimestamps.description: Map of status values to ISO 8601 timestamps, recording when each status transition occurred. Useful for measuring phase duration.
